claim.title: Colorado local-contact neuron
claim.lede: This neuron responds most strongly to Colorado Front Range local context: event listings, venues, public records, community services and contact lines, especially at a place name or the boundary before a 303/720/970/719 telephone number. Its output direction promotes Colorado, Denver, Boulder, Colo, Broncos and related local tokens. The response is not exclusively Colorado: a smaller token-level component also fires on some non-Colorado place names, numeric boundaries and code fragments.
claim.one_paragraph: Across 100 million tokens, product is centered near zero (median -0.029; 99th percentile 1.20), with a long positive tail to 322 and a shorter negative tail to -73.5. The top natural anchors are Longmont event listings, Boulder County farms, Denver sports and C.R.S. district resolutions; at the strongest, gate and value are both large (18.5 × 17.375 = 322). Controlled comparisons support a Colorado-local component: city-plus-303 `call` products were 86.5–126.0 versus 8.75–22.5 for matched out-of-state cities; Colorado venues reached 90.5–144.0 versus 0.87–20.1; Colorado area codes reached 141–191 versus 2.25–11.1. A Colorado venue without a phone still reached 191 at ` Colorado`, and a bare `City offices, 303-` reached 149, so neither cue is strictly necessary. Qualifying this account, 43 of 105 blind-labelled source-code points were positive (maximum 43.25), `大连` averaged 66.9, and some high positive activations occur in Kyrgyz text, so a narrower token/place-boundary component coexists with the Colorado effect.
claim.negative_pole: The negative pole is heterogeneous and is best treated as a departure from the Colorado-local contact pattern, not an anti-Colorado concept. The corpus minimum is -73.5 on `(` at the end of a long Chinese news prefix reaching a Xining/Qinghai dateline; the Qinghai `日报` anchor reaches -54 and the blind Qinghai candidate -52.75, with `环`, `省` and `县` also negative. Qinghai templates gave minima -25.9 to -36.8, below matched Xinjiang, Gansu, Sichuan and Beijing controls (-5.8 to -0.3). Highcharts `.data`/`.x` (about -43.5) and Montana or North Dakota civic contact records (-45.75 and -40.5) form separate mechanisms, so code and non-Colorado records do not collapse into one semantic category.
claim.what_would_change_my_mind: Non-Colorado local news or sports that reliably match the Colorado positive magnitudes would argue for a general local-information feature; conversely, Colorado venues and contact lines that fail under controlled templates would undercut the local-context account. A single coherent semantic or upstream mechanism shared by Qinghai, code and civic negatives would replace the heterogeneous-negative explanation.

response_rules.name: Colorado Front Range local context
response_rules.description: The full prefix establishes a Colorado Front Range locality or Colorado institution through place names (Denver, Boulder, Longmont, Fort Collins, Aurora, Berthoud, Niwot, Minturn, Fruita), area codes 303/720, C.R.S. citations, district resolutions, or local venues. The anchor may be a space, function word, digit, or phone-number fragment inside news, event, service, venue, or public-record text; the Colorado cue often appears earlier in the prefix.

response_rules.name: Colorado sports teams and athletes
response_rules.description: The prefix is a Denver-area or Colorado sports report about the Broncos, Rockies, Nuggets, CU, or local high-school/college teams and athletes, and the anchor introduces a player, team, game, score, or other sports detail. Explicit Colorado wording is not required when team names or the sports context identify the Colorado connection.

response_rules.name: Qinghai and Tibetan-plateau provincial news
response_rules.description: The full prefix is Chinese-language provincial or local reporting centered on Qinghai, Xining, Yushu, Sanjiangyuan, or Tibetan-plateau counties and institutions. The anchor falls on an administrative or place token (青海, 西宁, 省, 县, 日报, 环, 站长) or an adjacent punctuation or number within that report.

response_rules.name: Source code and chart markup
response_rules.description: The prefix is dense source code or JavaScript/library markup, especially Highcharts-style property and method chains such as .data, .x, .series, and .point, or similar script fragments. The anchor is a property, method, syntax, digit, or whitespace token inside that code context.

response_rules.name: Non-Colorado civic and contact records
response_rules.description: The full prefix is a U.S. civic, regulatory, or contact-directory passage tied to a state or agency outside Colorado, such as North Dakota legislative material, Montana BLM or ARM notices, or California/Oroville services. The anchor is a telephone-number digit, statutory citation number, address, or contact field, and no Colorado locality is established.

response_rules.name: No visible cue
response_rules.description: The prefix is generic prose, academic or mathematical writing, an ambiguous multilingual passage, or a mixed context in which neither the Colorado-local pattern nor a coherent negative cue can be established. Weak negative values in ordinary text also belong here.

criticism.attack: The account may mistake a general local-information or contact-directory feature for a Colorado-specific one. If the response is broader, non-Colorado local news, venues and contact lines should approach the Colorado positives.
criticism.prediction: Under matched local templates, out-of-state city and venue controls should be close to Colorado if the feature is generic; a large Colorado advantage would support specificity.
criticism.result: Colorado city names at the shared 303 `call` marker measured 86.5–126.0 versus 8.75–22.5 for Billings, Boise, Cheyenne and Salt Lake City; Colorado venues measured 90.5–144.0 versus 0.87–20.1. Colorado area codes also exceeded non-Colorado codes (141–191 versus 2.25–11.1). Controlled English specificity therefore survived, but the claim is narrowed by strong non-Colorado corpus positives: 43 of 105 blind-labelled source-code points were positive, reaching 43.25, and `大连` averaged 66.9. This is a dominant Colorado-local response, not an exclusive Colorado detector.

criticism.prediction: Area-code-only and number-free probes should discriminate between the explanations: area-only should match city-plus-number if numerics drive the response, while the no-phone venue should be low if a phone is required.
criticism.result: A bare `City offices, 303-` reached 149.0 over the scored span, below city-plus-number values of 175.0–251.0 but far above the non-Colorado number maxima of 2.25–11.1. Conversely, Longmont Public Library, Colorado, without a telephone number still reached 191.0 at ` Colorado`. Thus numeric contact details and Colorado place context both contribute, but neither alone explains the full pattern; the contact-line account needs qualification rather than replacement.

criticism.attack: The negative tail may be one coherent anti-Colorado or anti-local mechanism. If so, Qinghai news, source code and non-Colorado civic records should share a semantic cue and upstream contributors, and matched non-Qinghai provinces should be indistinguishable.
criticism.prediction: If the heterogeneous-negative account is right, Qinghai snippets should be more negative than matched other-province controls, while code and civic records should be negative through different local contribution patterns.

Highcharts `.data` and the Montana BLM number formed separate negative mechanisms with different upstream units. Zeros or weak values for several other administrative tokens and ordinary prose mean the negative categories are not equally strong, but there is no single opposing concept. The heterogeneous-negative claim survived as written.

criticism.attack: An adequate explanation should let an independent writer approach both corpus extremes without access to the expected answers. Failure on either pole would show that part of the response is missing from the account.
criticism.prediction: Blind candidates generated from the initial explanation should reach near the 322.0 positive maximum and the -73.5 negative minimum; a large shortfall would narrow the corresponding pole.
criticism.result: The blind positive writer reached 312.0, close to the 322.0 corpus maximum, and all six positive candidates were Colorado-local contact texts, supporting the positive account. The blind negative writer reached only -52.75 against -73.5 and did not reproduce the punctuation/Xining extreme. The positive pole is therefore supported, while the negative account remains incomplete and is narrowed to a set of heterogeneous categories. Route prediction was disabled.

criticism.attack: The frozen response rules should label the sampled corpus consistently if the Colorado account is complete. High positive products in source code or contexts labelled No visible cue would contradict a narrow Colorado-only reading.
criticism.prediction: Feedback labels from the initial claim should have high directional coverage and few high-magnitude sign errors; otherwise the explanation needs an explicit qualification.
criticism.result: Directional coverage was 31.5% (137 of 435 feedback points), with 67.2% accuracy among directional labels. Of actual-positive points, 44 were predicted negative, almost all source code, with positive products reaching 43.25; another 201 actual positives and 97 actual negatives were labelled uncertain. Kivy markup reached 36.0 and Kyrgyz prose reached 85.0 in the no-cue bucket. These are substantial mismatches rather than near-zero sign disagreements, so the revised claim adds a cross-lingual/token-boundary qualification and treats source-code negativity as a boundary case, not a rule.

sweep-001.title: Colorado city cue with a fixed 303 contact line
sweep-001.rationale: Tests whether Colorado place context adds to a constant 303 contact line. Colorado city names should raise the product at the ` call` marker above matched out-of-state cities, while generic local labels should be weaker.
sweep-001.caption: At the shared ` call` marker in a template ending with a 303 number, Longmont, Boulder, Denver and Fort Collins measured 124.5, 100.5, 86.5 and 126.0; matched Billings, Boise, Cheyenne and Salt Lake City measured 8.75–22.5. Generic `local neighborhood` and `community` controls were 0.74 and 1.13. Native product, single-marker scoring.

sweep-002.title: Colorado versus non-Colorado telephone area codes
sweep-002.rationale: Tests whether area-code identity alone carries the positive tail. Colorado 303/720/970/719 numbers should yield higher replacement-span maxima than matched 406/701/435/928 numbers, with extension and office controls lower.
sweep-002.caption: Within a fixed `call <number>` template, maximum replacement-span products were 188.0, 191.0, 141.0 and 159.0 for 303, 720, 970 and 719 numbers, versus 11.13, 6.03, 2.25 and 6.94 for 406, 701, 435 and 928. Extension and office controls were 0.16 and 0.19. Native product, maximum over the replacement span.

sweep-003.title: Qinghai news versus matched provincial and record contexts
sweep-003.rationale: Tests whether Qinghai provincial reporting is the specific negative cue. Qinghai, Xining, Yushu and Sanjiangyuan snippets should produce lower minimum products than matched Xinjiang, Gansu, Sichuan and Beijing snippets; code and Montana records should not reproduce the same effect.
sweep-003.caption: Across a fixed news-brief replacement span, minimum products were -27.75, -27.75, -36.75 and -25.88 for the four Qinghai/Tibetan-plateau snippets, compared with -5.84 to -0.26 for the Xinjiang, Gansu, Sichuan and Beijing controls. A Highcharts control reached -12.38 and a Montana 406 record -27.38. Native product, minimum over the replacement span.

sweep-004.title: Actual Colorado venues versus a mere Colorado mention
sweep-004.rationale: Tests whether genuine Front Range venue context raises the ` call` marker. Colorado venues should exceed matched Montana, Idaho, Wyoming and Utah venues, while a Colorado-themed business located in Montana and a location-free center should remain weak.
sweep-004.caption: At the common ` call` marker, four Colorado venue descriptions measured 144.0, 90.5, 123.0 and 108.5, while matched Billings, Boise, Cheyenne and Salt Lake City descriptions measured 0.87–20.13. A Colorado-themed restaurant in Billings measured 9.81 and a location-free community center 0.69. Native product, single-marker scoring.

sweep-005.title: Colorado area code alone versus Colorado context without a phone
sweep-005.rationale: Tests whether a Colorado area code is sufficient and whether local context without a telephone number is weak. Area-code-only, city-plus-code and Colorado-place-without-phone conditions should discriminate between numeric and place-context accounts.
sweep-005.caption: Maximum replacement-span products were 216.0, 231.0, 251.0 and 175.0 for four Colorado city-plus-number strings, versus 4.59–50.0 for matched out-of-state strings. A bare `City offices, 303-` reached 149.0, while a Longmont, Colorado, string without a phone reached 191.0 at ` Colorado`. Native product, maximum over the replacement span.

p1.name: Longmont golf-course contact listing
p1.description: A Longmont membership and event listing whose space before a 303 telephone number reaches product 304. Positive local RelP contributions are led by L38_N489 and L14_N489, with smaller positive contributions from L31_N11703 and L6_N25239; this is the clearest positive contact-line member.

p2.name: Boulder County farm report
p2.description: A Boulder County agriculture and Front Range flood report whose selected ` in` reaches product 290. It shares the positive L38_N489/L14_N489 signal but has a stronger L6_N7831 component, showing that the positive route also covers Colorado prose without a telephone number.

p3.name: Colorado running-club sports profile
p3.description: A Colorado Rage running-club and high-school sports profile whose selected ` At` reaches product 294. L14_N489 and L38_N489 are the largest positive contributors, with L49_N12697 and L13_N11715 also positive; this route covers sports and community biography rather than a contact record.

n1.name: Mixed Qinghai, civic, code and prose negatives
n1.description: This negative numerical route contains unlike members: Qinghai `日报` (-54.5), a Montana BLM 406-number digit (-45.75), Highcharts `.data` (-43.5), a Slamdance prose ` more` (-15.625) and a credit-repair period (-4.3125). L14_N8626 and L38_N8626 are negative contributors, while L6_N24380 and L6_N6972 change sign across members. The route is not a semantic class.

n2.name: Weak math-homework final period
n2.description: A single weak negative member: the final period of a math-homework post (-0.578). L6_N24380 and L6_N6972 contribute negatively, but the magnitude is small and the member is too isolated to support a semantic name.

n3.name: JavaScript polyfill syntax
n3.description: One JavaScript URLSearchParams polyfill member at a semicolon (-1.211). L6_N24380 and L6_N6972 contribute negatively and L52_N19157 also appears; the source-markup cue is clear, but the response is much weaker than the Highcharts example.

clusters.name: Colorado Front Range local and sports text
clusters.story: Membership criterion: positive selected products in Colorado Front Range text. The Longmont golf-course contact line, Boulder County farm report and Colorado running-club profile have different anchors and genres but share positive L38_N489/L14_N489 local contributions. This is a local-context cluster rather than one fixed template; the cross-lingual positives in the wider spectrum remain outside it.

clusters.name: Qinghai newspaper trailer
clusters.story: Membership criterion: Chinese-language text whose observed prefix reaches 青海日报 after a long mixed news page. The single member's 日报 anchor is negative, with negative L14_N8626/L38_N8626 and positive L6_N24380/L6_N6972 contributions. One member supports a Qinghai-media association, not a broad Chinese-language rule; matched other-province probes were much weaker.

clusters.name: Non-Colorado civic contact record
clusters.story: Membership criterion: a U.S. civic or contact record outside Colorado. The member is a Montana BLM lease notice ending at an out-of-state telephone digit; that digit is strongly negative and shares negative numeric contributions with other English records but not with Chinese text. It remains a distinct non-Colorado civic-contact boundary case, not evidence of an anti-Colorado concept.

clusters.name: Negative code and markup anchors
clusters.story: Membership criterion: two negative technical anchors, a Highcharts .data property and a JavaScript URLSearchParams semicolon. Their local contribution patterns differ in magnitude, and the wider blind-labelled spectrum contains many positive code points, so these members mark a negative boundary case rather than a general source-code rule.

clusters.name: Weak heterogeneous prose negatives
clusters.story: Membership criterion: remaining weak negative prose without a code, Qinghai or civic-contact account. Slamdance film prose, a credit-repair disclaimer period and a math-homework final period are semantically unrelated; their products are weak and upstream patterns do not identify a shared cue. This unresolved mixed cluster is retained rather than forced into a semantic story.

spectrum.summary: Across 495 blind-labelled spectrum points, the frozen rules assigned 55 Colorado-local, 11 Colorado-sports, 9 Qinghai-news, 105 source-code, 15 non-Colorado-civic and 300 no-visible-cue cases. Colorado-local and sports products were nearly all positive (up to 322), Qinghai uniformly negative (-10.5 to -38.75), while source-code and no-cue points crossed zero and included strong positives.

search.summary: Two saved search regions were tested. At the ` call` marker, six Colorado local-contact candidates had median product 7.26 (best 18.13) versus -0.22 for matched out-of-state controls. At `发布`, Qinghai candidates had median -4.37 (range -9.31 to 1.17) versus 0.005 for matched other-province controls. Fixed-template sweeps independently produced much larger Colorado city and area-code contrasts.

clusters.summary: Ten natural members form five display clusters: three positive Colorado Front Range texts, one Qinghai media trailer, one Montana civic contact, two negative code/markup anchors and three weak heterogeneous prose negatives. Route n1 crosses Qinghai, civic, code and prose, so route IDs are not semantic classes; code negativity is a boundary case, not a rule.

anatomy.summary: The gate-by-value view shows product as gate times value: the largest positive anchors combine strongly positive gate and value, while negative products arise mainly from positive gate and negative value. The selected strip separates the cue tokens, the boundary before the number and the upcoming value.
anatomy.strip_caption: Saved Longmont event-listing trace: gate rises to 18.5 and value to 17.375 on the space immediately before `303`, giving product 322. The preceding ` call` and Longmont tokens are positive; the scored location is the boundary before the upcoming phone number, not a token inside the number.

ablation.summary: `+1` product raises ` Boulder` (+0.743), ` Colorado` (+0.729) and ` Denver` (+0.722); strongest suppressions are `orbit` (-0.429) and Chinese fragments, not a coherent anti-Colorado set. Across 121 zeroing conditions median KL was 0.00226 versus 0.00039 for random controls; the Longmont phone-boundary case was much more sensitive (KL 4.56).

family.summary: Eleven authored inputs showed a controlled gradient: Colorado city plus 303/720/970 lines reached maxima of 186–292, matched out-of-state lines 4.8–29.5, and a Longmont text without a phone 111. A Qinghai-led prefix kept its 303 line negative (-42.25). Upstream units tracked place tokens and phone digits; downstream readers split by sign.

circuit.summary: Local RelP over fifteen atlas graphs concentrates upstream flow on L38_N489 and L14_N489, with L31_N11703, L49_N12697, L6_N7831 and L6_N25239 recurring. The thirty nominated readers split by sign, led by L62_N21256, L59_N9433 and L57_N16330; these are local associations, not causal routes.

tests.summary: Blind candidates written from the initial explanation reached 312.0 against the 322.0 corpus maximum; all six positive candidates were Colorado-local contact texts. The negative candidates reached -52.75 against -73.5, led by Qinghai, Highcharts, Montana and North Dakota examples, so the negative extreme was not recovered. Route prediction was disabled.
